A_target.statement:
Let $t$ be a well-typed term of the [[Definition:Simply Typed Lambda Calculus|simply typed $\lambda$-calculus]].
Then every [[Definition:Beta Reduction|reduction]] sequence starting from $t$ is finite.

B_source.statement:
Let $\struct {W, <}$ be a [[Definition:Well-Ordered Set|well-ordered set]].
Then there is no infinite strictly decreasing sequence $w_0 > w_1 > w_2 > \cdots$ in $W$.

substitutions.each term / reduction state: an ordinal (or element of a well-founded order) measuring it
substitutions.one reduction step: a strict decrease in the assigned measure

object_map.reformulation: Assign each term a measure in a well-founded order (via a reducibility/logical-relations argument) so that every reduction step strictly decreases it.

validity_conditions: One must exhibit a measure on terms landing in a well-founded order such that every reduction step strictly decreases it (the hard part, typically via reducibility candidates).
Given such a measure, an infinite reduction would yield an infinite strictly-decreasing sequence in a well-order, which is impossible.
proof_plan: Define a measure $\map \mu t$ assigning each well-typed term an element of a [[Definition:Well-Founded Relation|well-founded]] order, such as an [[Definition:Ordinal|ordinal]] or a multiset of type degrees of redexes.

Show that each reduction step $t \to t'$ satisfies $\map \mu {t'} < \map \mu t$.
For the multiset measure, contracting a redex of maximal degree creates only redexes of strictly smaller degree.
An infinite reduction sequence would give an infinite strictly decreasing sequence in the well-order, a contradiction.
